utterances.text: On this sketch, I see only numbers, and I don't know what clues were marked by the scene-of-crime officers by which numbers. I just know that one of these is the place of descent of one projectile and the spot marked on the rail tracks is the landing of the other projectile. Now, what the other numbers mean, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 16 at the same time, using the split screen? That's where the key is shown. Pages 16 and 17 on our split screen. Oh, then we need the sketch to remain on one half of the screen. This is page 16 that I asked for, and the sketch should remain on the other side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the report mentions there were two casualties, and that the place is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: My report mentions the place where the shell landed and where the victims fell, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it normal, in cases of homicide, that the position of the body is marked by a chalk, its shape is marked?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes, if the body is found on the spot when we arrive. Otherwise, there's nothing to mark. And I already said earlier that by the time we arrived on the scene, we would not find either the bodies of the killed or people who were wounded. And in this case, again, we did not find the bodies of the dead, so we were not able to mark their position. Our job was to record and present the crime scene as we found it, not as someone describes it. That's what we found. That's what we saw at the time when we were conducting our investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In our interview, and again I see in your statements, you said that if the crime scene had been changed, you would normally record it. Did you record in this report whether this crime scene has been altered and how?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I don't see it is written that the bodies had been taken away. It must be an omission on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you use the pencil again, if I may ask the usher to help, to mark the place where the first projectile landed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, I don't know anymore which landed first and which landed second, but I will try to mark the two projectiles. [Marks] I believe one is designated by number 2 here, and the second one [marks] could be the one marked by one, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Feel free to use this key. That's why we placed it on the screen. And can you tell us where the fuse was found, the fuse of one of the projectiles? Just look at the key, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I'm looking at my report, because that's the only thing that I'm responsible for. The key was made by the scene-of-crime officer. I would not to make any markings based on something I'm not entirely sure about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it written in your report that you found the fuse, in what condition it was, and where it was lying?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: It says that forensic inspection found fragments of the projectile, and the place of descent, that it was taken over by the MUP, and that it would be submitted to experts. So in my report, it says that examination by scenes-of-crime officers of the place where the projectile landed found fragments of the projectile. They were taken over by members of the bomb squad of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they would be sent for further examination. So I did not describe in detail which fragments were found. And it goes without saying that a fuse is also a part of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that here, under number 9, it says: "Part of the fuse"? So on the picture, under number 9 is the place where part of the fuse of the projectile was found?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: That's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you then put a circle around this "9." Because there is no translation of the key, we would know that it's where the fuse was found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We do have the translation of the key. It's page 7 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now put the date and your number there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]. It's not a problem. Would somebody remind me of my number?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. When we have an English translation, this was not necessary. But, in any event, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D862, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D2163.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with that place, you frequented it before; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Which place?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The place where the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2163, please, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know this street? Is it Danila Ilica Street, nowadays called Oprkanj?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes, I know this street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark, roughly or exactly, the spot where the projectile, or at least one of the projectiles, landed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: That would be really difficult now to remember and to mark. My report says it's somewhere in that street, but would I be able to remember exactly whether it is close to the curb?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]. I find it hard to remember anything with certainty, but I think it's not far from the curb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the same again; put the date and number.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D863.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 40 of the previous document, 13172. Page 40. Page 40 in the 65 ter 13172. We had that document on the screen a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- can you recognise this window?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I cannot remember it. It's just a fragment of a wall and a window.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you remember it from your file? It's written below. Can we zoom in a bit further.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: It says that it's a protective metal window with damage on it, damage from explosion. It's possibly a window on this street. I think it's in Danila Ilica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your job was to record the evidence?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: To record and mark the evidence. Photo documentation, photographs, and video footage are the job of the scenes-of-crime officer. I just indicated it in the sketch, but it was not my job to photograph this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who told him to photograph the window, and who made these markings in chalk?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I cannot recall now. It was too long ago. I cannot remember who ordered him to take pictures. If there are markings, then they must have been made by the scenes-of-crime officer or the ballistics person. They would have been recorded also on the sketch, together with the markings of other damage and other clues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But all this is going on under your supervision, correct, under the supervision of one of the leaders, and you said it was your responsibility to record evidence?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: No, I said it was my responsibility to put together a team and to enable each member of the team to do his part of the job. It was not my job to tell them what to mark, what not to mark, how to photograph or film it, and how that would look on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation for the fact that there are no -- there is no fragment damage on the wall, just chalk marks?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I cannot give you no such explanation [as interpreted]. I believe the experts from the bomb squad could give you the explanation of the effects of such an explosion and how the fragments would be scattered. All I know is that on some sides, there would be more fragments; on another side, less. But you need an expert to give you that sort of explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have page 41 of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the previous photo, you couldn't see marks on the wall, and they were not marked in any way, either; only on the window?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see everything that was marked and what traces are visible on that photograph. I can't do that on this photograph, either.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's bring the previous picture back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that the shutters are open? This is that same window, and it's now the shutters are open; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: That's what it says in the caption below the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you see any markings or traces on the wall in this one? First, let's look at the first picture. Do you see, on any of these photographs, fragment traces on the wall? The fragments that damaged metal must have left some traces on the wall as well.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I don't know if I can see very well. I mean, I'm using glasses, but from what I can see, there are some circles on the black background. I don't know if that is the damage represented in the comments below the photograph. I'm not sure if that's what I'm seeing or not. But, anyway, on the -- in the text below the photograph, it states that the metal protective area of the window does indicate damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it on the window. Those places are marked in chalk. But we have no traces on the wall of any fragments -- made by any fragments; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Again, I'm telling you that I don't see if there are any or not, and I don't see them marked. I don't know whether there were any or not. And if there were any, I don't know why they weren't marked. I really think these questions should be directed to the person who created these photo documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- for 25 minutes. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at page 35 in this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting: Witness, sir, how has this scene changed in the meantime, other than removing the people who were killed? To what extent has the scene of the incident been altered?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I really couldn't say, because I don't know what it looked like initially, especially because in my report, I failed to note all the things that were altered. But based on my experience from that period, usually the scene was altered to the extent that those who were killed or wounded were removed, and that would be the information that we would get from the local police. I don't know if anything else was altered or not. I couldn't know something like that, so I had to rely on what was conveyed to me by the local policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the ground or the soil around the crater cleared, within the crater? Did anybody inform you about that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to recall such details. It's been a long time since then. I really cannot remember. I wouldn't be able to confirm that or deny it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I ask the usher, please, to turn the marker on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can I ask you to link up these rocks or stones and these parts of something from the top of the photograph down. But those that are lying on the periphery of the center, do you see those objects in the photograph? You can see them in the upper top left-hand corner. There's one, two, three, four, five, six, or seven pieces or so. Could you link them or connect them with one line, please?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]. If that's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, all right, these are the closest to us. Well, would you agree, when you look at it, that these fragments are in a convex shape -- concave in relation to the top and convex in relation to us? Perhaps let me say that again in our language, like my adviser says. So is this depressed part facing away from us and the one that is convex towards us?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: The part that is bulging is facing the crater, it's facing us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Is that what is marked with number 2 the place where the projectile hit the curb of Oprkanj Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, the curb of the Oprkanj Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have an explanation why these fragments are not facing us, why the shape those fragments are making is not reverse than what it is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I really cannot comment on that. I'm not an expert, and I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Could you put your initials and the date on this photograph so that it can be tendered.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we tender this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D864, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 36 of this same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is that same location; is that correct? It just says: "Crater photographed from close up." So we can see the pipes that are shown in the previous photograph, but the image is not so close up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say, Yes, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said, Yes, that is what it states in the caption underneath the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 37. So it's just one page ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you notice the pattern of the soil that you can see there? Can we zoom in, please. Can you please read out what it says underneath this photograph.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: "The same crater photographed after the clearing of the material that was scattered around, with marked damage created by the explosion."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What do we see here? We see the compass and the number 1?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, I see the number 1. I don't recognize what is to the right of the number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you can see that the soil has been removed and cleared here, is that correct, just like it is written at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes, it says at the bottom of the photograph that the material that was scattered around was cleared.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we move on to the next page, please, 38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I wonder what the point of this line of questioning is, this and the previous half hour before the break, looking at photographs. The witness hasn't been able to add anything, other than read the description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Quite true, Mr. Hayden. I don't see the point, Mr. Karadzic. This is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I will, then, tell you, and I will disclose my Defence case before this witness. Everything was altered here, and nothing was conducted in keeping with the standards of on-site investigations. And we have before us one of the leading persons working in these teams, and this is the person who should explain whether an on-site investigation should be conducted in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You could put that question easily to the witness, for the first thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what these hands, the compass hands, indicate?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I don't know what they indicate. All I can do is read the caption below the photograph, which says that the arrow shows the direction -- the incoming path of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, it was put to you that everything was altered here, nothing was conducted in keeping with the standards of on-site investigation. What would you have to say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that once my team arrived on site, they did everything as prescribed by the law. It was not pointed out, in any specific terms to me, what it was that we failed to do according to the standards of the profession. The only thing was, and we failed to mention that, that the bodies of the casualties were -- and the wounded persons were removed from the scene. So I could not infer from the question what it was that was missing, because in the last question, apparently the suggestion is that nothing was done according to procedure, so I would like it to be pointed out to me and then I can comment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, with the Trial Chamber's patience, and if you can just bear with me, I will show what my direction of questioning is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, the scene of crime was altered; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, only in the sense that the bodies of the casualties were removed. Everything else is as recorded in the report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 1D02178.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us whether the clues or the traces on the ground were altered in any way?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I don't know what traces you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we've just heard now that the crater was cleared and that the soil was disturbed.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, I can only comment and say that I assumed that the crater was cleared after the KDZ team, the bomb squad team, examined the scene and stated what kind of condition they found it in. And you can also see that from the photographs. You could see the photographs made before the clearing of the area and after it was cleared. In other words, it was done in stages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at this photo, and just disregard the arrows and the numbers there. Can you observe that these are the photographs of the same scene, and we see that the ground or the soil was disturbed, and that there are no traces of any fragments on the ground there that would indicate the direction of the -- the incoming path of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, all I can say is that these photos were taken from two different angles. Now, whether any fragments were there or not, and what the bomb squad experts and ballistics experts recorded in their reports about the crime scene, I really can't comment on. All I can observe here is that these two photos were made from two different angles and that the magnification degree was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see that the ground was disturbed and the soil was not in the same spot where it was in reference to the curb?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, I don't know when the first or the second photos were taken, whether they were taken immediately upon arrival on the scene or after it had already been examined and documented. So whether, in photograph 2, the number indicates the soil or anything else, I don't know. I cannot really go into commenting this because I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think that was a fair question to the witness. Can we bring up page 37 of the previous document, and English version page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that these two photos were photos of the same site from two different angles?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait. If we look at the English translation, it says that it's the same photo of the close-up projectile crater, but crater photographed after debris was cleared away. It's clear from the caption. So what is your question, Mr. Karadzic? The investigative report, itself, says it cleared the debris. So that's what you referred to as being altered. Can you confirm that's what it says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what it says in the original as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that a crime scene may not be altered before it is examined and documented? Could you answer with a yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, I can't be as brief in my reply. All I can say is that the same site, the same crime scene, is photographed at various stages at first, when we just arrived, and then at the second and third stages, after certain measures were taken. So, in other words, photographs can be taken at several different stages, and that is true of this photograph as well. And probably the photo file contains the crime -- the scene of crime as we found it originally, and then this one after it was cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How is the incoming trajectory of a projectile determined?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I'm sure that that's a question for an expert in that field, and I am not such an expert nor am I familiar in detail with what methods they use in order to determine the incoming trajectory and path.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that the layout of the traces around the crater has to be preserved and should not be removed before it's examined? You were the person who documented the recovery of evidence on the site, so why was the site cleared away before you arrived?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, I can't really see, from this photo, whether the trajectory was already established and then the crime scene cleared away or whether it was done the other way around. I can't see it, based on this photo. This is probably a question you should put to the author of this photograph and to the people who conducted the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Three points, Your Honour. One, the witness has now stated on a number of occasions that he is not familiar with the methods of determining trajectory or direction of fire. Second, the accused has stated in his question: "Why was the site cleared away before you arrived?" The witness has already made it clear that that's not the case, it was only the bodies that were removed before he arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably the Chamber has allowed too much for cross-examination of this witness to the accused. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpretation was -- Your Excellency, it's quite all right. This is a large case and involving many incidents. The interpretation was bad. I asked, What was altered before on the ground, and then my question was, Why was it necessary to clear away the soil from the crime scene? So we are having difficulty here with the interpretation, and I will have to obtain the video materials in order to check them at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would like to know this: Did you make sure that each member of your team carry out their work properly, because that's what you stated in your statement, and why, then, did you allow the soil to be removed, and that was a determining factor in establishing the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, again, I have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He answered your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we then have 1D2164, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please indicate, on this photograph, the point of impact of the second shell. Is this where it landed, and could you please mark the spot where it was? But do not use the marker that you have there. Could the witness please be provided with a pen, a regular pen.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: This is a new photograph, and it approximately depicts the area. However, I can only mark approximately the place where that projectile would have fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, can you just do it approximately?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: No problem, I will try to indicate where that was [marks]. I think it's about here somewhere, but please don't take my word for it. It's not 100 per cent precise, but it's approximately in this area here, because this is a later photo and in the meantime the street was repaired, the stores are different and they were changed, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please date this and put your pseudonym number.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will not discuss this incident at length or as much as I wanted to, because I won't be able to ask you about many of the things I'm interested in. Could we now please have page 44 of the earlier document, and I would like to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D865.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unfortunately, because of technical difficulty, we lost the picture. Could you mark it, kindly, again, Mr. Witness, and sign it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D865.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, who could answer our questions in relation -- regarding this incident? Who is the person who could answer all our questions? Who was the person responsible for the investigation into this particular incident, so that we can put all our questions to them? Could you -- you don't have to use a name. Could you just tell us the job title of that person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: That's not an appropriate question, Your Honour. The witness, for a start, can't possibly know what kind of questions Mr. Karadzic has regarding this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Previously, you answered, Mr. Witness, that Mr. Karadzic should put that question to the author of this investigation report. Do you know who the author was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The part relating to the photo file and the sketch of the scene of crime, as well as the video-recording of the scene of crime, is the person indicated there as the scene-of-crime officer. As for the questions about the incoming trajectory and the angle of descent, and other matters that relate to the explosion, itself, I assume -- or, rather, I'm sure that a bomb squad expert would have all the answers to those questions, because that would have been the person who conducted the investigation and tried to establish what kind of projectile was in question. So each individual would be responsible for their own field of expertise, to answer the questions relating to that field of expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And as regards the timing to clear the crime scene after having investigated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please be more specific? Do you mean the clearing away after everything was completed or does this relate to the earlier question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For example, whether or not to clear the debris from the crime scene after proper investigation, and when to do it, who decides that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I could see the method of the bomb squad experts and the way they work, I saw that first -- what they do first is establish and determine -- describe the exact situation as they found it when they arrived. Then they determine the angle of descent, and once that is done, they would clear away the debris from the point of impact, itself, and I assume this is done because it is expected that other parts of an explosive device or projectile that had come in could be found. So that is done at that stage. There is a stage called the "clearing of the debris" stage, but I cannot tell you exactly what that pertains to because that was done by the individuals who are responsible for that part of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why would, then, the marking of the direction from which the projectile came, on page 38, take place after the marking of the crater and the scene -- after the clearing of the crater, correcting. The interpretation is a disaster. I apologise to the interpreters. We're probably speaking too fast, but the interpretation is confusing. After the clearing of the crater, the direction of fire is determined. Does that mean that the traces are not important or even make it harder to determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I believe we're coming back again to the answers I've already given. I don't know their methods. Perhaps we should look to see if there is a photograph taken before the clearing, and how it was taken, not look at the photo file selectively, but look at the entire photo file to see if there was a photograph before, just when the team came to the site, and then you can maybe get an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this document, itself, it is written on page 38 and it is shown that the direction was determined. May I now ask for page 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic -- no, I will stop you. Your question was on the basis that the photos in this investigation report were compiled in chronological order. How can this witness answer that question? You said you would move on to your next topic. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, I want just one more photograph so the witness can confirm. It's directly within his purview. Page 44 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Until then: Witness, can you tell us who is answerable for this case, for this documentation? Who is responsible at the moment when this documentation is submitted to the Prosecutor's Office? Who is the author of this document, as a whole?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I've said that the author of the photo file is the scene-of-crimes technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Who is responsible for this case? Who is answerable for this whole case file? It is submitted to the Prosecutor's Office with the intention of bringing the perpetrator to justice. Who is responsible, who is the end author who makes the synthesis and submits the file with the intention of bringing the perpetrator to justice?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: The synthesis of all the material that has been made, the findings, the traces, et cetera, was done by the department called at that time the Genocide Department. Based on that material, they wrote up a criminal report that was submitted to the Prosecutor's Office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The whole department or a person in that department whom we can call? We can't call the department. Who can we call to shed light on this case?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge about the method of work, on every criminal report given to the Prosecutor's Office, there is the name of the person who processed the case, who worked on it. So probably on their document, you can find the identification of the person who put together the whole material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Witness, in all these cases, whenever we try to pin-point someone who is responsible, they slip away like soap. Can you mark on this picture the fuse? These are fragments that you recorded. Could you mark the fuse on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I don't see anywhere a document where it says that I recorded and gathered these fragments. In my document, it says, and we can come back to it again, that fragments were found. There is not a single word or a sentence in my report that says that a fuse was found or any other specific fragment by name. Again, I repeat, I am not the person who knows or is able to identify the fuse on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We saw, in the key under number 9, that there was a fuse. If we have a fragment of fuse on this photograph and you're unable to mark it, we can move to the next incident. Did you investigate the incident in Safet Hadzic Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I was in Safet Hadzic Street, but it would be good if you could tell me which incident happened there and what it was all about. And I'm telling you, again, I did not conduct the whole investigation, but the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then get -- just a moment. We have an ERN number here. 65 ter, it would be, 09784, without broadcasting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this official report?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes. My name is on it, but there must be another two pages of it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the next page to see who signed it, page 3 from here. This is the first in Serbian. We need the third.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see who signed it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes. That's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at that page, and then we should go back to the front to see all you need. Tell us when you need to go back to page 2 or 1.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: You can start asking your questions while we're on page 3. I don't know what you wanted to say by -- what you mean by saying, Look at what you need. I have no idea what your questions are going to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Because I'm going to ask you about another case, I wanted you to refresh your memory using this document so I can call up something else into e-court. Can we see page 2. Thank you. We will call them every time, or perhaps we can have the Serbian version of this document printed out so we can call up other things. Can we print pages 1, 2 and 3 and give the witness a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness has a hard copy with him now. That's what you said, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent. I didn't know that. No, I wanted him to have it now. Does he have it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have this report on paper?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent, thank you. Can we now get 10273.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting: Witness, before which number in Safet Hadzic Street did this incident happen?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I believe my report speaks about, if I can put it that way, events of two kinds. An event is described where activation of explosive devices was found, as written in my report, from a 90-millimetre gun, and the impact of a modified air-bomb on a residential building. If you mean Safet Hadzic Street, and it was -- it used to be called the 1st of May Street, an explosive device of huge destructive power impacted outside number 152. But also in the same street, outside numbers 110, 102, et cetera, damage was found caused by a projectile fired from an artillery gun, or, rather, several projectiles fired from artillery guns of 90 millimetres and one projectile of great destructive power, which was a modified air-bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what happened outside number 52? Because you also list that number.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: It says "on the roof," so there must be a mistake here, a typo. Either number "1" was typed by mistake before "52," or perhaps "1" was omitted before "52." In any case, it's a typo, because there was only one projectile of huge destructive power. Now, at this moment, after all this time, I cannot tell you whether the correct house number is 152 or 52. In any case, it was about one residential building and one roof. Now, in view of what happened, and in retrospect, to view our work in this way, as if we had worked under ideal circumstances, and to expect me to explain how an error occurred, I cannot. It is a typo, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark which projectile fell on which building? Use green, please, or black. You can change the colour on that pen.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: If I can remember correctly now, it's this one [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put number 1 and tell us what fell there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]. I think this explosive device of great destructive power or, as I wrote down, modified air-bomb, fell on this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did this German Nazi shell fall, whatever you found?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: It's written exactly, what impacted there, and there is a description. I'll try to draw a line to mark, approximately in this area [marks], damage was found in several places from these artillery projectiles. If my memory serves me well, this is a school and these are residential buildings. And on this axis, damage was found, including one unexploded shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The black line is number 2; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that denotes the layout of fragments from another projectile?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Not fragments, but damage caused by several projectiles that fell there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what is this building just behind number 2?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I just told you. If I remember well, it was a primary school. I believe it's still a primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what was it during the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what's that building further towards the top with two big windows? Or, rather, is that a transformer station in Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Possibly. Possibly, there was a transformer station near this streetcar depot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put number 3 on that building.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this transformer station for Novi Grad feeds everything that's important in Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I have no idea what areas are fed by this transformer station and which area it covers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Again, could you please put the date and your number.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What you said was the school, could it have been a police station in Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. May this document be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D866, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D02198, please. 1D02198.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, do you see the building of the television station here, then the transformer station, the Surveying Institute? Can you just mark them and say, Number 1 is this, number 2 is this? Can you see the TV building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put number 1 there, in whatever colour.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Surveying Institute?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: It's together with the Municipal building of Novi Grad, if I can combine both the Municipality building and the Surveying Institute at number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see the police station at Novi Grad? Is the red roof at the police station?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you see the transformer station better now?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether this is perhaps the transformer station. I can mark it, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Put number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks] But I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just mark the building on which the projectile impacted? Formerly, 1st of May Street, nowadays Safet Hadzic Street.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: This is the photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the school?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: It could be this building [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put number 4?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how the direction of fire was determined here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to look in your report to see what's written there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: It says that if we are talking about this modified air-bomb, it says that the direction is south-south-west, that it came from that direction, which corresponds with the positions in the area of Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But here, at the beginning of page 2 -- or, rather, the end of page 1, it says: "The projectile fell not far from the north-western wall of the residential building in Safet Hadzic Street." Can you draw an arrow to mark this north-western wall of the building? You know where the north is, you know what it looks like. Can you draw a line -- or, rather, an arrow to show the north-west direction.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I don't know if that's right [marks], but the north-western part of the building is on this side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I wanted to let you know that you have spent so far two hours and a half, and you will have one hour left. So plan the remainder of your cross-examination to cover everything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's the source of the greatest frustration for the Defence. We are dealing with important witnesses and important documents, and a large number of incidents, so we cannot just muddle through it and rush through it. In cases where there was a rush through such things, people have been convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at your report. Based on unexploded projectiles and the detected parts of exploded projectiles, it was established that they were always armoured projectiles, 90-millimetre calibre. Can you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, about this north-west wall, can you connect it -- or, rather, can you extend this line, this arrow you drew, across the entire photograph?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put the date and your number.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D867.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you continue? It says here that you also found a shell produced in Germany, with an eagle, with a swastika. Can you read that: "Calibre, 90 millimetres, produced in Nazi Germany ..."

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: "With the following markings."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Go on until "Ilidza."

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: "The sign of eagle with the swastika, WOA411." And then in the extension number, "3." "Eagle with swastika," and opposite that, number "1." And then "CZL," and below, "BYW." And then opposite that, "043," and below that number, "968." And in extension letter "A."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that three such projectiles were found, or is it one?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: If I can remember well now, it was one unexploded projectile. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "Explosive artillery projectiles, calibre 90 millimetres"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: It says there were several of them that landed and exploded, and this one was found unexploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the next sentence: "According to the traces --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "According to the traces, it was established that all these projectiles from a weapon so far undetermined were fired from the direction of the west, which corresponds to the positions of the Serbs." How did you come to this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: That's a question for the members of the team. If you have before you the first page of my report, those are persons under numbers 3 and 4, especially the person under number 3. That was his field of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who is the ballistics person in this investigation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: You can probably see, yourself, that not a single person here is identified as a ballistics expert or a member of the bomb squad team, so there were probably none of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how was the conclusion made in Bascarsija, in the previous incident, that the shell came from Mount Trebevic, from the Serbian positions? What was the decisive criterion enabling you to say that it came from the Serbian positions on Mount Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Asked and answered. He's already stated that he doesn't know about the methodology and how it was determined. He only recorded the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, that on Trebevic, the forces of the BH Army held several hills and several important features just overlooking Bascarsija at Colina Kapa, Mala Kapa, then further on Debelo Brdo, et cetera; is that so?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I told you that today or yesterday when we talked, but I had never been at the lines, nor do I know in which areas members of the BH Army were positioned or members of the VRS. And I cannot tell you now where the BH Army positions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that for a while you lived at the very separation line in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a question that might --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you don't have to. It cannot have any effect, but I withdraw my question. Do you consider that a team that is supposed to establish the direction of fire, it is very important to know the disposition of the forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think it's for the witness to answer that, such a question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Excellency, it says here that the projectile had come from the aggressor side, the rebel Serb forces. I will overlook what it says here, "the Serb rebel forces," but there is an identification of a perpetrator and a location of where they were, so we have to know where that was if that's what is stated in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that so, Witness? If you say that a projectile had come from a place, here or there, that would mean that you know where it had come from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the witness answered that he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, why, then, did you put your signature on this report, where it says that the place from which the projectile had been fired was identified and who had fired it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I may put your cross-examination to a stop if you continue to ask such a question. Move on to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now briefly look at P1058, please. Can we zoom in on the central portion of this. Or, rather, my apologies, leave it as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is a map of the chief of staff of the 12th Division Command? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: The witness has previously answered that he had no contacts with the ABiH, did not visit any of their positions, had no contact with the military. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But by chance, he may have noticed. Can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not really the person who can confirm whether this is a map of the chief of staff. I mean, it does say so on the map, itself. It says, at the bottom right, "Chief of staff," Colonel So-And-So. But whether this indeed his map or not, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a Prosecution exhibit, so there is no reason to doubt it. Now, could we zoom in on the part of the map, the area where several incidents took place, and tomorrow we will clarify some other parts. Could we zoom in a bit further, the entire area below. A bit further, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the television building here, please, and Safeta Hadzica Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, the print is too fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see, at "102," there's the wire factory, and that's where the television building is? Are you familiar with this part of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Well, all I can do is read that below number "102 bbr," it says "Goranka" neighbourhood, but perhaps the television building -- it's too small here, but it's possible that it's to the left of the digit "1" in the number "102."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm asking you again whether it is a proper and efficient use of time putting such question to the witness, who says -- who is not familiar with the military situation. You can use this map in your submission, as much as you can, later on. What's the point of putting this question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the final conclusion of your investigation was? You can take a look at the report. Can we have 1D2143. I consider it very important for this witness to be able to place the incident and its location. Now, we will have to play this, because it hasn't been up-loaded into e-court. If you allow me to play 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: It's not for Mr. Karadzic to prove or disprove this incident to this witness. Therefore, it's not appropriate to have him show to him where this position is, as Mr. Karadzic has just stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show this map from our computer. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, would you please mark the same buildings, the television building, the factory, here on this map? Can you see it now? Or, rather, can you see the map of this place before you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm told that it is not possible to mark on this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it possible to save it as it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see now the incident site?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: I cannot. What I see before me, on my screen, is just a form to enter case numbers, and description of case, and so on. Now I can see it. I can see the facilities that you wanted me to mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, could you then, please, put a circle around Geteova Street and then the incident site?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I was told that it's impossible to mark on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, do you agree with me, then, that the television building can be seen here, as well many factories, as well as two incident sites, the Geteova Street and the Safeta Hadzica Street incidents?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you investigated those two incidents, as well as the third one on the building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, and if you have a hard copy, you can ask the witness to mark on the hard copy. I note the time. We'll adjourn for today. And you have to finish your cross-examination in 35 minutes today [sic]. Mr. Tieger, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In light of the cross-examination today, I'd just like to note that the next witness, as I related earlier, has been in The Hague for a considerable period, accommodating both the requests by the Defence -- scheduling adjustments. If we don't conclude tomorrow, he'll obviously have to be here until Tuesday. I would note that for the purpose of encouraging, if at all possible, the completion of his evidence tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may respond. I would request that -- at least one session tomorrow for this witness. And we were allowed four hours for the next witness, which is insufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, you have to finish in half an hour tomorrow. And we are supposed to sit from 9.00 to 2.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I had checked -- let me check the schedule once more. I didn't note that, but that's good to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll check the court schedule now, but we'll see how we can manage. Mr. Witness, have a nice evening. But during the adjournment, you are not supposed to discuss your testimony with anybody else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is now adjourned. Tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of November, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
